sections.h2: Does South Carolina have an estate tax?
sections.html:
No. The South Carolina Department of Revenue states that South Carolina has no estate tax for decedents dying on or after January 1, 2005.

That means an heir who sells an inherited South Carolina house does not owe a state estate tax return before the sale can close. The page we opened addresses the estate tax only, so we do not make a statement about other state death taxes. Ask the Department of Revenue or a probate attorney if a specific question comes up.

The federal estate tax is a separate system. The IRS lists a filing threshold of $13,990,000 for deaths in 2025 and $15,000,000 for deaths in 2026, measured against the gross estate plus adjusted taxable gifts and the specific gift tax exemption.

sections.h2: When does a federal estate tax return matter for a house?
sections.html:
Only a large estate must file a federal return, so most South Carolina families selling an inherited house will not. The IRS says simpler estates with cash, publicly traded securities, easily valued assets or jointly held property generally do not need to file.

A return can still be worth filing for a different reason. Since January 1, 2011, a decedent's estate may elect to transfer any unused exemption to a surviving spouse, and the election is made on a timely filed estate tax return.

sections.h2: What does an estate owe in South Carolina income tax after a sale?
sections.html:
The estate itself may owe income tax, and it files the SC1041 fiduciary return. A resident estate or trust must file if it must file a federal fiduciary return, has any South Carolina taxable income, or has a nonresident beneficiary.

The Department of Revenue lists other triggers too: gross income of $600 or more, or any trust with taxable income. Nonresident estates and trusts must file if they have income or gain from South Carolina sources.

  • The return and the payment are due by the 15th day of the fourth month after the tax year ends.
  • Filing extensions run up to five and a half months, but the Department says there is no extension of time to pay.
  • Estates and trusts must generally withhold on South Carolina income distributed to nonresident beneficiaries.
  • A liability of $15,000 or more per filing period must be filed and paid electronically.

A house sale may produce gain that flows through this return. Our South Carolina capital gains guide explains the 44 percent deduction that estates and trusts may use.

sections.h2: Who has the power to sell an inherited house in South Carolina?
sections.html:
The personal representative can sell, once appointed by the probate court. Under S.C. Code Section 62-3-701, the duties and powers of a personal representative commence upon appointment.

Section 62-3-715 allows a personal representative acting reasonably for interested persons to acquire or dispose of an asset, including land, at public or private sale, and to sell, mortgage or lease estate real property for cash or credit. Those powers are subject to a contrary will or court order and to Section 62-3-711(b).

Section 62-3-711(b) adds a limit: a personal representative may not sell real property except as authorized under Section 62-3-911 or the court procedures starting at Section 62-3-1301, unless the will authorizes it otherwise. Read the will first, because a sale power written into it can change what court steps are needed.

A buyer is protected. Under Section 62-3-910, a purchaser for value from a personal representative acting under a will's sale authority takes title free of the rights of heirs, devisees and other interested persons, and the same protection reaches a purchaser from a distributee holding a deed of distribution.

sections.h2: What probate deadlines affect the timing of a sale?
sections.html:
The creditor and contest periods set the clock, and several of them run for eight months or one year. A seller who knows these dates can plan the closing date.

  • Inventory: the personal representative must file an inventory and appraisement within ninety days of appointment, listing probate property at fair market value as of the date of death.
  • Creditor notice: the representative publishes notice once a week for three weeks in a county newspaper, asking creditors to present claims within eight months after first publication (Section 62-3-801).
  • Outside limit: claims that arose before death are barred unless presented within the earlier of one year after death or the notice period (Section 62-3-803).
  • Contesting informal probate: a contest may be filed within eight months of informal probate or one year after death, whichever is later (Section 62-3-108).

Claims secured by a lien on estate property are not cut off by those limits, so a mortgage or tax lien stays on the house until paid at closing. Section 62-3-909 also requires a distributee who received property improperly to return it, which is another reason to settle the estate with care before heirs split the proceeds.

sections.h2: Which closing costs follow an inherited house sale?
sections.html:
The deed recording fee is $1.85 per $500 of value, made up of $1.30 for the state and $0.55 for the county. The grantor is generally liable, and the buyer is liable second.

A deed from a personal representative is not on the exemption list we read, so plan to pay the fee unless an attorney finds an exception. Exemptions listed include corrective or quitclaim deeds that confirm title already vested with no consideration, and deeds in lieu of foreclosure to the mortgagee.

The real property tax bill is the other bill that follows the house. Sumter County's Treasurer, for example, says property taxes are paid one year in arrears, with notices each October and a January 15 payment date before penalties begin. Ask the county where the house sits for its schedule.

sections.h2: What problems do heirs run into with a South Carolina house?
sections.html:
Heirs often have to carry a house with no one living in it while probate runs. Taxes, insurance and utilities continue, and so do repair needs. Section 62-3-703 asks the personal representative to settle and distribute the estate as expeditiously as is consistent with the estate's best interests, so a slow, costly carry is something a representative has reason to avoid.

  • Several heirs who disagree on whether to keep or sell
  • Heirs living out of state who cannot visit the property
  • A house with deferred repairs the estate cannot fund
  • A tenant in a rental the decedent owned
  • Unpaid taxes or liens that must clear at closing

We buy houses as-is, including inherited properties, and we work with the personal representative's attorney on the paperwork. A written offer lets the heirs compare a cash sale with a listing that would first require repairs and cleanout.

Before you accept any offer, confirm that the personal representative has been appointed and has authority to sign. Expect the closing attorney to ask for proof of the representative's authority, and have the court's appointment papers ready.

faqs.q: Does South Carolina have an inheritance tax?
faqs.a: The Department of Revenue page we opened says South Carolina has no estate tax for deaths on or after January 1, 2005. It does not address any other state death tax, so confirm with the Department or a probate attorney.

faqs.q: How much can an estate be worth before the federal estate tax applies?
faqs.a: The IRS lists a filing threshold of $15,000,000 for deaths in 2026 and $13,990,000 for deaths in 2025.

faqs.q: Can an heir sell the house before probate ends?
faqs.a: Only the personal representative can sign for the estate, and the representative's powers start when the court appoints them. Section 62-3-711(b) restricts selling real property unless Section 62-3-911, the court procedures starting at Section 62-3-1301, or the will authorizes it.

faqs.q: How long do creditors have to make claims against an estate?
faqs.a: Notice is published once a week for three weeks and asks creditors to file within eight months of first publication. Claims arising before death are barred after one year from death, or sooner for creditors given notice.

faqs.q: Who files the estate's income tax return?
faqs.a: The fiduciary files Form SC1041 when the estate has South Carolina taxable income, gross income of $600 or more, or a nonresident beneficiary. The return and payment are due the 15th day of the fourth month after the tax year ends.
